messages:
maya: Heads up — we're seeing a spike of DSAR deletion requests tied to snapshots in eu-west1. Several jobs are failing on KMS decrypt with `AccessDenied`. Paging legal and infra.
jonah: Logs? exact error code? can you paste the decrypt call?
maya: Paste from worker logs: ```2026-04-06T10:01:02Z ERROR plugin.kms: Decrypt failed -> AccessDenied: Caller not authorized for kms:Decrypt on projects/…/locations/global/keyRings/redwood-eu/cryptoKeys/snap-enc (resource="projects/…")```
sec-bot: [alert] 1 critical KMS AccessDenied events in eu-west1 · https://console.example/traces/abc123 :eyes:
alejandra: Did we push the RBAC tweak earlier for the snapshot-cleaner SA? I rolled a minimal change ~09:35 but only to staging.
maya: I made a hotfix around 09:50 to remove `roles/storage.admin` from a service account that had been over-privileged — I thought it was only for metadata access. Could that have cascade?
jonah: If the SA lost the kms:decrypt IAM binding (or the key's IAM had a condition), decrypts will fail. Check IAM policy for that key and the IAM bindings on the SA. Also check if key is in a different project with cross-project binding.
ops-runner: Running quick query: ```gcloud kms keys get-iam-policy snap-enc --location=global --keyring=redwood-eu --project=redwood-prod```. Replying in 2m.
ops-runner: Result: policy shows binding for `serviceAccount:snapshot-cleaner@redwood-prod.iam.gserviceaccount.com` was removed at 2026-04-06T09:49:12Z (audit-id d3f4).
maya: That timestamp matches my change. I didn't touch KMS bindings explicitly. Might be an automated reconciliation job?
alejandra: We have a reconcile job that prunes stale bindings when a SA loses a tag. Could be a policy condition matched.
jonah: For immediate mitigation: (1) restore kms:Decrypt on the SA for that key, (2) re-run the pending DSAR deletion queue replayer to finish deletions, (3) mark affected requests for legal with audit evidence.
lia (Legal): Priorities — DSAR timelines: we must acknowledge within 7 days, complete deletion where applicable. If decrypt fails we need to document the failure and an extended timeline. Please attach per-request evidence showing attempted deletion attempts + KMS error.
maya: Will do. Plan: revert the reconciliation change that removed the binding, re-run a canary of 10 deletions into a test key, validate Tombstone->Deleted state. Then requeue backlog.
jonah: Also add an audit marker to logs when DSAR handlers start, so `subject_request_id` shows up in KMS request/metadata. That will help prove attempts in case of escalation. Example header we can add: `X-DSAR-ID: sr-<id>` and log it before Decrypt.
ops-runner: Quick workaround if restore will take >30m — we can route DSAR jobs to the backup key `snap-enc-fallback` that still has the SA binding. Small script: ```# requeue to fallback
python tools/requeue_dsars.py --from-key snap-enc --to-key snap-enc-fallback --limit 200```
alejandra: Long-term: tighten reconcile to never remove KMS bindings unless key-owner workflow approves; add unit tests for reconcile job to detect DSAR consumers.
lia (Legal): Please create a record in the DSAR tracker for affected request IDs and include KMS audit entries. I'll draft the customer message template if we need to extend timelines.
maya: On it. I'll restore binding, kick canary, and post results here. ETA 20m. :clock10:
sec-bot: [audit] iam.policy.change detected — actor: maya@redwood, diff: removed binding serviceAccount:snapshot-cleaner at 2026-04-06T09:49:12Z
jonah: After restore, let's also run a quick vuln-triage: make sure this change wasn't exploited. Search for `kms:Decrypt` success logs from other actors during that 09:40–10:05 window.
maya: Update: restored binding at 10:12, canary of 10 deletions succeeded (all transitioned to Deleted). Requeue starting now. Sharing audit excerpt in infra ticket.
lia (Legal): Thanks — collect all proofs and keep me posted for any customer outreach.
ops-runner: backlog requeue in progress — 482 items. Monitoring token consumption and errors. Ping if anything spikes.
jonah: Follow-ups: (a) add DSAR header to KMS calls, (b) fix reconcile rule unit tests, (c) postmortem with timeline and approval gating.
maya: Agreed. I'll open the postmortem and tag eng-security + infra + legal. Closing here once backlog drains or we hit errors. :white_check_mark:
